pl-l3d20c1-d1e117.summary: Answers whether God could free man otherwise than by Christ's death: another way was possible to God, to whose power all things are subject, but there was no other, and should have been none, more fitting for healing our misery. Nothing so lifts our minds and frees us from despair of immortality as God's valuing us so highly that his unchangeably good Son, remaining what he was and taking from us what he was not, deigned to share our condition and bear our evils by dying.
claims: God could have freed man otherwise.
No way was more fitting than Christ's death.
Christ's death frees us from despair of immortality.
